title: Document
description: A parsed source document: an optional scope header plus its declarations.

scope.description: The scope header, if the document opens with one.

Annotation.description: Provenance attached to a lore-bearing declaration.

condition.description:
Optional hypothesis condition under which the claim is asserted
(`assumes <hyp>`).

span.description: Where the annotation appears in source.

tags.description:
Further provenance tokens carried verbatim — an agent id, a session tag,
a scene cue. Retained so nothing on the line is dropped (koan 4).

AtomExpr.description: A predicate applied to a list of argument terms, e.g. `adjacent(a, b)`.

subject.description: The entity the slot is about.

BodyLiteral.description:
One literal of a rule body: an atom on a polarity rail.

A positive literal ([`negated`](BodyLiteral::negated) is `false`) joins over
the relation and binds its variables; a negated literal filters against the
certain layer and binds nothing (datalog safety: every variable in a negated
literal must also appear in a positive body atom).

negated.description: Whether the atom is negated (`not <atom>` at the surface).

CitationRef.description: A reference to a decision-ledger entry, e.g. `D-0042`.

Clause.description: One normalized interior line of a keyword-fronted block.

span.description: Where the clause appears in source.

CondExpr.description: A boolean condition over named hypotheses that gates a claim.

ConditionDef.description: A side condition: `condition seated-reading requires phase(turning-leaf) within declared-span`.

modulus.description: The cycle modulus, if written (`cycle tide(4)`).

spokes.description: The ordered spoke names around the cycle.

Datalog.description:
A datalog derivation rule: one head atom and its body conjunction of
literals. Produced by the front end from a `head :- body` clause; consumed by
the evaluator's typed rule intake.

body.description: The body conjunction of literals (a negated literal is `not <atom>`).

head.description: The head atom derived when the body holds.

Decl.description:
A top-level declaration.

The gentle subset — [`Entity`](Decl::Entity), [`Attr`](Decl::Attr),
[`Fact`](Decl::Fact), [`Question`](Decl::Question), [`Before`](Decl::Before),
[`Hypothesis`](Decl::Hypothesis) — is fully typed. The expert tier keeps a
typed header and a captured [`Clause`] body.

oneOf.description: `<subject>.<attr> = <value>` — a slot fact about an entity.
`rule <name> [over <domain>] …` — a checker rule (world, order, or season).
`variant <path>` — a lore variant of an artifact.

EffectDef.description: What a casting does: `effect invoke degrades acquaintance by 1`.

form.description: The form whose casting carries the effect.

kind.description: Which kind of entity this is.

slots.description: Indented slot facts written beneath the entity.

ErrorClassDef.description:
A declared diegetic failure, refining a structural class:
`error wrong-turning refines L3 side-condition [timing] over cycle turning-leaf`.

class.description: The structural class, or [`None`] if `refines_token` names none.

discriminant.description: The discriminant — the sub-case detail after the class token, verbatim.

name.description: The failure name (the drama the scene voices).

on_resource.description: The resource an `L6` failure spends against (`… on <resource>`).

over_cycles.description: The cycles a timing failure is seated on (`… over cycle <w1>, <w2>`).

refines_token.description: The token written after `refines` (`L3`, or whatever malformed thing).

signal.description: The on-mic signal a performer voices when it fires (`signals <x>`).

triple.description: Whether the surface used the leading `fact` keyword (triple form).

FileId.description: Identifier for a source file within a compilation.

body.description: Any other captured body clauses (`suppose …`, `add fact …`).

GradeDirection.description:
The single declared direction a [`ResourceKind::GradedMonotone`] grade moves.

A graded order is written `whole > worn > husk`; the `>` reads as "wears
down to", so the default and the series-canonical direction is [`Decays`]
(`docs/spec/04-practices.md` §4 — "nothing is spent, knowing only *wears*").
The opposite is admitted so the algebra is symmetric: a grade that may only
climb its order is [`Grows`].

[`Decays`]: GradeDirection::Decays
[`Grows`]: GradeDirection::Grows

oneOf.description: The grade only ever moves *down* its order (negative deltas): it wears.
The grade only ever moves *up* its order (positive deltas): it ripens.

Ident.description: A named identifier with its source span.

span.description: Where the identifier appears in source.

implies.description: The atom this option implies, if written.

PracticeBody.description:
The typed interior of a [`PracticeDecl`](crate::decl::PracticeDecl) body
(LS-9): the retained raw clauses plus the structured [`PracticeDef`].

The parser is the single producer (via
`dli_syntax::structure_practice_body`); `dli-ledger` reads
[`def`](PracticeBody::def) without re-entering the front end. The raw
[`clauses`](PracticeBody::clauses) are kept so the formatter round-trips the
surface byte-for-byte — the typed `def` is lossy against the written text.

clauses.description:
The whitespace-normalized interior clauses (one per physical line), in
source order. Retained verbatim so the formatter reproduces the surface.

def.description:
The structured practice, produced by the front end from `clauses`.

Boxed to keep the [`Decl`](crate::decl::Decl) enum small (the many-field
`PracticeDef` would otherwise dominate every declaration's size); the box
is transparent to serde and the JSON Schema, so the stored carriage bytes
are unchanged.

body.description:
The typed body: the retained interior clauses plus the structured
[`PracticeDef`](crate::practice::PracticeDef), pre-parsed by the front end
(LS-9, `docs/design-notes/lorestore-roadmap.md`). `dli-ledger` reads the
typed structure without re-entering `dli_syntax`.

PracticeDef.description:
A compiled practice: the workbench's typed view of one declared law-set.

Everything that distinguishes one practice from another lives here as data
(charter koan 10); the generic checker and evaluator read this and nothing
else. The cycles that were in scope at compile time are recorded on
[`cycles_in_scope`](PracticeDef::cycles_in_scope) so reference resolution
needs no further environment; the front end produces the structure with an
empty `cycles_in_scope`, and `dli-ledger` overlays the document's cycles when
it compiles the practice.

costs.description: The currency vocabulary a casting may spend in.

cycles_in_scope.description:
The cycles in scope at compile time (those the document declares), against
which cycle references are resolved. The engine seats no ambient cycles —
a world's cyclic vocabulary is declared, never baked in (DL-0017). The
front end leaves this empty; `dli-ledger` fills it at compile time.

marker.description: The provenance marker the declaration carried, if any.

resources.description: The resources and their algebra laws.

uses.description: The layers this practice consumes (`use language.registers`).

head.description: Remaining header tokens (`family plot mission pass`).
Remaining header tokens (`speaker protagonist in spoken-proof`).

ProvenanceMarker.description:
The leading provenance word a claim carries.

A claim's *standing* is not stored (DL-0003: there is no status slot); it is
derived from this marker together with the citations behind it. The marker
records only where the claim came from — an agent's proposal or a ledger
ruling — and which register of ruling it was.

oneOf.description: `proposed` — an agent's claim, awaiting a ruling. Carries no citation.
`provisional <d-id>` — a provisional ruling, open to revision.

ResourceDecl.description:
A declared resource and the closed-algebra law it obeys:
`resource acquaintance(name) : graded monotone whole > worn > husk`.

The [`kind`](ResourceDecl::kind) is the closed-algebra tag; it is [`None`]
exactly when the declared law is not a member of the algebra, which
well-formedness surfaces as a compile error. The law's parameters — an affine
[`cap`](ResourceDecl::cap), a graded [`order`](ResourceDecl::order) and
[`direction`](ResourceDecl::direction) — ride here alongside the tag.

cap.description: The affine capacity expression, verbatim, for `affine bounded <cap>`.

direction.description: The direction a graded resource wears (`>` reads as decay).

kind.description: The closed-algebra law, or [`None`] if the declared law is outside it.

law_text.description:
The law phrase as written, kept for the error message when `kind` is
[`None`].

order.description: The graded order, most-whole first, for `graded monotone <order>`.

ResourceKind.description:
The conservation law a resource obeys — the closed algebra, as a tag.

This enum is closed on purpose (spec §6, second well-formedness obligation):
a resource whose kind is not one of these members is a compile error, because
there is no open resource vocabulary. The law's *parameters* — an affine
cap, a graded order — are not stored here; they ride on the resource
declaration and are passed to the semantics functions explicitly.

conserved.description:
Whether the multiset must net to zero across the close (no mint, no
burn), on top of the never-negative discipline every linear resource
keeps.

oneOf.description: `affine bounded <cap>` — spent at most up to a declared capacity.

`graded monotone <order>` — an ordered grade that only ever wears in one
declared direction.

RoleDef.description: A cast role: `role reader : entity requires standing(reader)`.

requires.description: The standing conditions the role requires, verbatim.

sort.description: The sort a filler of this role must belong to.

clauses.description: The structured block-body clauses (indented or braced), in source order.

inline.description:
The inline `head : body` clause carried on the rule line itself, present
only when the header holds a `:`/`:-` separator and the block body is
empty. It is rendered from the header tokens, never as a body line, so
the surface round-trips; the loader reads its structure here.

RuleClause.description: One structured clause of a rule body.

clause.description:
The whitespace-normalized clause text and its span. Retained so the
formatter round-trips exactly and the order/season domain engines read
their own micro-grammar off it without re-entering the front end.

datalog.description:
The world-rule datalog structure, present when this clause is a clean
`head :- body` (or `head : body`) derivation rule. `None` for an
order/season domain clause or a clause that is not clean datalog — the
world loader turns a `None` in a world rule into a malformed-rule
finding, exactly as it did when it re-parsed the text itself.

body.description:
The typed body: world-rule datalog pre-parsed into
[`Datalog`](crate::rule::Datalog); order/season clauses retained as text
for their domain engines (LS-9, `docs/design-notes/lorestore-roadmap.md`).

domain.description:
The domain the rule is enforced over: `None` is a world rule, `over order`
an episode-ordering constraint, `over season` a season-ledger rule.

head.description:
Header tokens after the name (and any `over <domain>`), before the body
(e.g. `severity error`, or the inline `head : body` datalog tokens).

RuleDef.description: A law of the practice: `rule lay(figure, leaf) requires phase(turning-leaf) = leaf`.

args.description: The head argument sorts/variables, in order.

form.description: The form the rule concludes (the head predicate).

RuleDomain.description:
The domain a `rule` is enforced over, routing it to the right checker engine.

A rule with no domain is a world (derivation) rule; `over order` routes to the
episode-ordering engine, `over season` to the season-ledger engine. The three
forms unify the surface under one `rule` keyword (the domain is stated, not
keyword-encoded).

ScopeHeader.description: A `scope <name>` header naming what the document's claims are about.

SortDef.description:
A declared finite sort: `sort figure = the-tide | the-weir | …`, or a sort
drawn wholesale from a consumed layer: `sort binder from lexicon.loan-words`.

source.description: The layer the sort is drawn from, when written with `from <source>`.

variants.description: The enumerated members, when written with `= a | b | …`.

Span.description: A half-open byte range within a single source file.

file.description: The file this span points into.

name.description: The state name (may be dotted, e.g. `gwern.water-status`).

value.description: The value the state takes, if written.

StructuralClass.description:
The seven structural error classes the checker knows.

Every diegetic failure a practice declares is a *refinement* of one of these
(`docs/spec/04-practices.md` §2). The classes are the closed target set that
well-formedness obligation 1 checks against: an `error` refining anything
else does not compile.

oneOf.description: L1 — unknown-form: the casting names a form the practice does not declare.
L2 — premise-not-available: a required premise is absent or contradicted.
L3 — side-condition: a declared condition fails (timing, consent, scope).
L4 — bad-instantiation: a form is instantiated against forbidden sorts.
L5 — invalid-chain: a step joins premises the law does not license.
L6 — resource-violation: a spend breaks the resource's algebra.
L7 — close-mismatch: the close does not follow from the accounted ledger.

Term.description: A term: a variable, symbol, literal, or time reference.

oneOf.description: A ground symbol naming an entity.
A reference into the time domain.

TimeClause.description: A temporal clause attached to an entity or fluent.

oneOf.description: `since <event>` — holds from the named event forward.
`until <event>` — holds up to the named event.
`< a < b < c` — an era precedence chain rooted at this entity.

TimeRef.description: A reference to a named era or event on the timeline.
